canonical_question: What temperature ranges beyond room temperature have been experimentally verified for the long-term stability and mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaZr refractory high-entropy alloys in reticulated structures?

question_variants.question: What is the temperature range of the 'compression tests' beyond 'room temperature' to ensure the 'reticulated structure' remains stable at service temperatures?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text explicitly states that compression tests were conducted at 'room temperature'. It does not mention any temperature range beyond room temperature or provide data on the stability of the reticulated structure at elevated service temperatures.

answers.answer: The text indicates that tests were performed at room temperature only. There is no evidence in the supplied spans regarding the temperature range beyond room temperature or the stability of the reticulated structure at service temperatures.
evidence_spans: Fig. 1 shows the X-ray diffraction patterns of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZr 0.5 . HfMoTaTiZr is identified as a single-phase BCC crystal structure (cI2-W), which is identical to HfMoTaTiZr prepared by Juan et al. [20]
The shape of the (200), (211) and (220) peaks are asymmetric due to the compositional difference between dendrite and interdendrite regions.
The XRD-determined lattice parameters of HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 are a HfMoTaTiZr = 3.392 Å and a HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 = 3.325 Å, respectively.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: There is no current experimental evidence in the provided literature defining specific temperature ranges for the stability or mechanical performance of the HfMoTaTiZr reticulated structure beyond room temperature.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The single available approach in the dataset is a negative characterization of the literature's scope, identifying that investigations were confined strictly to room temperature compression tests.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The stability and mechanical behavior of the reticulated structure at service temperatures (extreme conditions) are currently undefined and dependent on data that has not been generated or reported in the source material.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No contradictions exist as there is only one data point which establishes a boundary of 'no data' rather than conflicting observations.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Weak for the target property (high-temperature stability) due to the complete absence of high-temperature experimental data; strong for the limitation that only room temperature data exists.
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: The complete absence of high-temperature mechanical testing or stability analysis for as-cast HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloys in reticulated structures.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: Refractory HEAs with a reticulated structure likely maintain structural integrity at elevated temperatures due to the high melting points of constituent elements, but this cannot be verified without experimental data.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Perform compression and microstructural stability tests on as-cast HfMoTaTiZr reticulated structures at incremental temperatures starting from 500°C up to the intended service temperature of the power plant application.
